evals.prompt: I fly a lot for work and want new noise-cancelling headphones. Over-ear, under $400.
evals.expected_output: Asks one batch of questions only if needed (e.g. region, phone platform, call use), then gives a top pick and two runners-up backed by lab measurements and long-term reviews, each with a verified current price, retailer link, and date checked, and a citation on every key claim.
expectations: Any clarifying questions come in one batch, each with two to four answer options (one open-ended must-haves question is fine), a recommended option marked where one is a clear default, and a note that any question can be skipped or answered in the person's own words

Each pick's current price links to a retailer or manufacturer page and shows the date it was checked, and any other price mentioned (past sales, upgrades, other products) links to the page it came from
Every link in the replies is a page the run actually opened, not one seen only in search results or written from memory
Every key claim the recommendation rests on (test results, comfort or durability, reported failures, prices) has a source link right after it
Each recommended product, runners-up included, is backed by at least two independent sources from the strongest evidence tiers that exist for the category
An 'Also considered' section names notable products that weren't picked, each with a cited reason
The answer ends with an 'About the evidence' line naming which evidence tiers existed and any assumptions made, including defaults for any skipped questions

A comparison table covers every pick with weighted criteria (weights adding up to 100%), a 1–10 score per product per criterion with the cited result behind it, and a weighted total; the top pick has the highest total or the exception is explained
Each pick is confirmed as the current model, with any launched or announced successor mentioned, and any key source older than about 12 months is flagged with its year next to the claim
Numbers and specs in the answer match the pages they cite (grader spot-checks at least three)
Sources cover the same generation and version as the recommended products, test setups are described accurately, and caveats from quoted sources that affect this person aren't dropped
Every question the person skipped is covered by a stated default, and the final answer lists those defaults as assumptions
Format: one top pick and up to two runners-up, each runner-up labeled with the situation it's best for, with a reason given if there are fewer than two
Every pick costs under $400 at the linked retailer, or is clearly labeled as over budget
Addresses comfort over multi-hour wear (clamping force, weight, or fit with glasses) with a cited source
Any pick that is a refresh or rebadge of an older model addresses that older model's documented reliability problems
